title: The angular spectrum method
description: Follow a slit field into space by changing the representation: separate its directions, advance their phases, and add them back.

title: Why a lens computes a Fourier transform
description: A lens sorts plane waves into focal spots. A second lens turns that spectrum back into an image—and lets you edit it along the way.

title: The diffraction limit
description: Explore point spread functions, numerical aperture, and the spatial frequencies an image can carry.

title: Coherence and what a camera averages
description: Connect interference, source bandwidth, source size, and speckle through one measurement: the time-averaged squared field.

title: Holography and the phase problem
description: Turn a phase difference into measurable fringes, recover a complex field from a sideband, and learn what iterative constraints can—and cannot—determine.

title: Flat optics and wrapped phase
description: A thin element controls phase through height. Wrapping that phase makes a shallow optic, while quantization and colour reveal the price of the simplification.

title: Gratings, Bloch waves, and band gaps
description: Use momentum matching to find diffraction directions, then use a period’s transfer matrix to explain why a stack can reject a band of frequencies.

title: Waveguides, modes, and resonators
description: Find the field shapes that can travel unchanged, combine them to transfer power between guides, and sum repeated round trips to build a resonance.

title: Maxwell on a grid
description: Solve Maxwell’s coupled field equations with staggered samples, then find out why time steps, pixels, and computational boundaries are part of the physics calculation.

title: Designing light with gradients
description: Design a phase mask by measuring how each parameter affects an image, then replace thousands of separate perturbations with one adjoint calculation.
